verdict: Johnson Controls grew sales 10% to $7.11B and profit from continuing operations more than tripled to $967M, as data-center demand pushed Americas orders up 58% and backlog to a record $23.0B.

segments.name: Americas
segments.note: Building systems across the Americas — sales up 14% on applied HVAC and controls strength, with data centers driving a 58% organic jump in orders and a $17.8B backlog.

segments.name: EMEA
segments.note: Europe, Middle East and Africa — reported sales dipped 2% (up 3% organically) amid Middle East conflict pressure.

segments.name: APAC
segments.note: Asia Pacific — sales up 12%, led by applied HVAC.

opex.name: Selling, general and administrative
opex.note: The field organization that sells, installs and services building systems, plus the back office.

opex.name: Restructuring & impairment costs
opex.note: Costs of simplifying the company — far below last year's $400M.

otherDetail: Net financing charges of $82M, partly offset by $8M of equity income from joint ventures.

takeaways.title: Orders are surging
takeaways.text: Orders rose 44% organically across the company — 58% in the Americas — and backlog hit $23.0B, up 43%, on sustained data-center demand.

takeaways.title: Margins expanded everywhere
takeaways.text: Americas segment EBIT margin rose 250 basis points to 20.1%; all three segments expanded margins on operating leverage and better mix.

takeaways.title: Last year had the charges
takeaways.text: Much of the profit jump is arithmetic: the year-ago quarter absorbed $400M of restructuring and impairment costs, versus $87M this year.

oneTimers: Restructuring and impairment costs were $87M this quarter — a real cost, but far below the $400M taken in the year-ago quarter.
footerNote: Figures are for continuing operations, as Johnson Controls presents them; net income attributable to Johnson Controls was $967M after $3M attributable to noncontrolling interests.
